How to read this. Each section is a menu tab of the app, in sidebar order. Inside it, one diagram per screen or task, from the first click to where the flow ends or hands off.

The shape tells you the kind of step and the colour tells you who does it (see the sixteen shapes below). Dashed boxes that say Continues in are links: click one to jump to that diagram. Type any button label or screen name in the search box to find every diagram that uses it. Drag a diagram to move it; use Full screen for the big ones.

No diagram mentions that. Try a button label, a screen name or an agent name.

Overview

How to read the diagrams, the whole site map, and one request from referral to decision.

The sixteen shapes

The shape says what kind of step it is. The colour says who does it. Every diagram in this document uses only these.

Start

Where the flow begins: a sidebar click, a link, an event

End (done)

The flow finishes normally

End (stopped)

The flow stops: blocked, declined, cancelled, nothing to do

Screen

A page the person sees

Pop-up

A drawer, modal, menu or panel on top of a screen

Person clicks

A person's click, tap, key press or signature

Person enters

A person types, picks, drops or uploads something

System step

What the app does: validate, calculate, update the screen

FLO / agent

Automated work by FLO or one of the agents (Reader, Scribe, ...)

Decision

A yes/no or multi-way branch; every exit is labelled

Data saved

A record is created or changed (case, request, referral, mapping, rule)

Document

A letter, brief, report, appeal, form or file produced or read

Outside party

Payer, referrer, EMR or portal: something outside Psyflo acts

Wait

Time passes or the flow waits on someone

Message

A toast, banner or notification the person sees

Continues elsewhere

Jumps to another diagram; the label names it

Blue: a personPurple: FLO and the agentsGrey: the appOrange: outside partyAmber: decisionTeal: data savedCream: screenGreen and red: the ends

Global shell › Top bar › Three controls and how drawers close

      
The top bar holds three controls: the Demo menu, the 'Ask FLO' button and the 'Notifications' bell. The two drawers close the same three ways. There is no search box and no page title in the bar.

Global shell › Top bar › Ask FLO › Ask a question

      
Open the drawer, pick a suggested question or type one, and read FLO's answer. The suggestions follow the screen the person is on. FLO answers from the demo data after a short pause. What it says for each kind of question is in the next two diagrams.

      
The chat lives in the page, not in the demo data. It survives closing the drawer and changing pages, and 'Reset demo data' does not clear it. Reloading the browser does. The suggestions are worked out when the drawer opens, so a case page names its own case and payer.

Global shell › Top bar › Ask FLO › What FLO answers

      
FLO lowercases the question and tries its rules in order. The first rule that matches answers, so a question with two key words gets the earlier answer. Counts, names and the request or denial it points to come from the live demo data. Only the Cardinal answer is fixed text. Five rules read the screen the person is on and are drawn in the next diagram.

      
Typed questions use the same rules as the suggestion chips. Most rules ignore the page; the five on the next diagram use the open case page when the question does not name a case. Every link opens a view that matches the answer. PRD 08 describes row-level citations, thumbs and an escalate action on each answer; the demo gives one paragraph and one link instead.

Global shell › Top bar › Ask FLO › Answers that read the screen

      
Five of FLO's rules read the demo data for one case, one payer or one screen: what is missing, when an authorization ends, what a payer requires, which reviews are due, which patients need a fix before billing. When the question names a case ('R-1042') FLO uses it; otherwise it uses the case page that is open; otherwise the request that needs you first. Each answer names the case, quotes live data and ends with a link to the exact place. They are recommendations, never payer facts.

      
The short line 'This is FLO's reading of the demo data, not a payer confirmation.' appears once, under the answers that read payer rules, coverage or an authorization. The numbers and the wording are computed when the question is asked.

Global shell › Demo menu › Fast-forward the demo clock

      
Fast-forward moves the demo clock by an hour or a day. It changes what is worked out from the clock: ages, countdowns and 'overdue' wording. The one thing it can start is Verify's automatic re-check of a patient whose re-check came due.

      
The clock starts at Tue 20 Oct 2026, 10:42 am. It has no 'back' button: only 'Reset demo data' returns it.

Global shell › Addresses › Old links, redirects and pages that do not exist

      
A few old or short addresses are sent on to the page that replaced them, and anything the demo does not know opens a 'Page not found' screen inside the normal sidebar and top bar. Redirects replace the address, so the Back button skips over the old one.

      
In the single-file build the address lives after a '#'. The hosted preview has no address bar, so it keeps the route in memory and the same rules apply.

Dashboard › Summary from FLO › What the three lines say and where they lead

      
A compact card under the headline. FLO works three short lines out from the live demo data: who needs you and what is due soonest, which authorizations end within 7 days, and which denial deadlines fall this week. Each line has a link to the screen it is about. It is a recommendation for a person to check, not a payer fact, and it ignores the filters below it.

      
The wording and the numbers are computed each time. Nothing in the card is typed by hand.

Dashboard › Request drawer › Needs you and write-back boxes

Payers › Every pop-up › Save, discard, close

      
One page for how every Payers pop-up closes. Nothing is saved by closing: Cancel, the X, Escape and a click on the dimmed area all throw away what was typed, with no 'are you sure'. Escape closes only the top layer, so a menu, then the pop-up over a drawer, then the drawer each take one press. There is no undo; a saved edit is reversed by editing again, and the edit log keeps the old text.
